messages:
ken: Noticed increased onboarding errors again. Support says users copy the README curl multi-line with \\ continuations and when GitHub soft-wraps it the pasted command breaks (lots of 401s and “command not found”). Also some users on fish shell hit a weird var expansion issue.

ken: Current README curl snippet looks like:

ken: ```
curl https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```

ken: When the backslash gets a trailing space or a soft-wrap, terminals run the next line as a new command. Fish users reported they needed braces around the var and pasted literally got `$REDWOOD_API_KEY` which failed.

sam: Ugh. We should remove multiline backslashes from the quickstart and add a one-line curl plus Windows cmd and PowerShell variants. Also add a short fish note: use ${REDWOOD_API_KEY} or export in fish with `set -x REDWOOD_API_KEY your_key`.

sam: Proposed one-liner (cross-shell friendly):

sam: ```
curl -sS --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --header 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses --data-raw '{"input":"Hello from curl"}'
```

sam: Windows cmd variant (note %VAR%):

sam: ```
set REDWOOD_API_KEY=your_key_here
curl -sS --header "Content-Type: application/json" --header "Authorization: Bearer %REDWOOD_API_KEY%" https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses --data-raw "{\"input\":\"Hello from cmd\"}"
```

sam: PowerShell variant: use $env:REDWOOD_API_KEY

sam: ```powershell
$body = '{"input":"Hello from PowerShell"}'
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses' -Method Post -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $env:REDWOOD_API_KEY"; 'Content-Type' = 'application/json' } -Body $body
```

ivy: While updating docs, can we also fix a couple SDK parity things? The quickstart still shows `client.chat()` in Node + Python in a few places; new canonical calls are `await client.responses.create({ input: '...' })` and the Node import changed to `import Redwood from '@redwoodai/sdk'` (not the old package name). Those mismatches are causing noisy TypeErrors in the first hour of signup.

ivy: Node example to use in README:

ivy: ```js
import Redwood from '@redwoodai/sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const res = await client.responses.create({ input: 'Hello from Node' });
console.log(res.output);
```

ivy: Python async example:

ivy: ```py
from redwood import Redwood
import os
client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = await client.responses.create(input='Hello from Python')
print(resp.output)
```

ken: Add a tiny Troubleshooting note under quickstart: "If a pasted curl fails, try the one-line example. Check your shell's env var syntax (bash/zsh: $VAR, fish: ${VAR} or use set -x, cmd: %VAR%, PowerShell: $env:VAR)." Link to the shell table.

docs-bot: Created issue #8201: "docs: quickstart - replace multiline curl, add cmd/PowerShell/fish notes, and update SDK snippets to responses.create" 4DD https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/8201

sam: I'll open a small PR with the one-liner, the three shell variants, the fish brace note, and replace the old JS/Python snippets. Tagging @ivy for SDK parity check.

ivy: Will review and run the samples locally. :thumbsup:

ken: Thanks — should cut down a bunch of support noise.
